issues.failure_explanation: The proof of Proposition 3.1 asserts that for the Lyapunov operator $\calL = \fI_n \otimes \fA + \fA \otimes \fI_n$, its smallest singular value satisfies $\sigma_{\min}(\calL) = 2\sigma_{\min}(\fA)$. This claim is false for general Hurwitz matrices, including normal matrices with non-real eigenvalues. For example, for the normal Hurwitz matrix $\fA = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 10 \\ -10 & -1 \end{bmatrix}$, $\sigma_{\min}(\fA) = \sqrt{101} \approx 10.05$, so $2\sigma_{\min}(\fA) \approx 20.10$, whereas $\calL$ has eigenvalues $-2, -2, -2 \pm 20i$ and thus $\sigma_{\min}(\calL) = 2$. With error $\fE_\ell = \fI_2$, the residual is $\fR_\ell = \fA + \fA^\T = -2\fI_2$, giving $\|\fE_\ell\|_2 = 1$, whereas the claimed bound gives $\frac{\|\fR_\ell\|_\Frob}{2\sigma_{\min}(\fA)} = \frac{\sqrt{8}}{2\sqrt{101}} \approx 0.1407 < 1$, violating the bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace $2\sigma_{\min}(\fA)$ with $\sigma_{\min}(\calL)$ or a valid, computable lower bound on $\sigma_{\min}(\calL)$, which is generally computationally demanding for large-scale systems and eliminates the advertised $\calO(n)$ computational guarantee.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition 3.1 and Theorem 3.4 (the stopping criterion and certified accuracy guarantee for Algorithm 1) fail to bound the true error. Downstream claims relying on computing an $\calO(n)$ certified error bound for general Hurwitz $\fA$ are uncertified.
issues.title: Invalid Lyapunov error bound based on false singular value identity for Kronecker sum
issues.why_classification: A valid repair replaces $2\sigma_{\min}(\fA)$ with $\sigma_{\min}(\calL)$, which cannot be computed in $\calO(n)$ for large-scale matrices $\fA$, causing the primary complexity and efficiency guarantees of the error estimator to materially worsen.

issues.failure_explanation: In the proof of Theorem 3.5, the inequality $\fw^\T \tilde\fE\fA_j^\T\fw + \mu\fw^\T\fA_j^\T\fw \le \|\fw\|_2^2(\sigma_1(\fA_j)\|\tilde\fE\|_2 - \sigma_n(\fA_j)\mu)$ erroneously presumes that $\fw^\T\fA_j^\T\fw \le -\sigma_n(\fA_j)\|\fw\|_2^2$. The quadratic form $\fw^\T\fA_j^\T\fw = \frac{1}{2}\fw^\T(\fA_j + \fA_j^\T)\fw$ is bounded by $-\lambda_{\min}(-\frac{\fA_j+\fA_j^\T}{2})\|\fw\|_2^2$, which can be arbitrarily smaller in magnitude than $\sigma_n(\fA_j)$. For example, for $M=1$, $\fB_1 = 0$, and $\fA_1 = \begin{bmatrix} -0.01 & 100 \\ -100 & -0.01 \end{bmatrix}$, $\fA_1 + \fA_1^\T = -0.02\fI_2 \prec 0$ and $\kappa(\fA_1) = 1$. With $\fX = \fI_2$, error $\tilde\fE = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0.001 \\ 0.001 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$, and $\mu = \kappa(\fA_1)\|\tilde\fE\|_2 = 0.001$, the matrix $\fA_1\hat\fX + \hat\fX\fA_1^\T$ has $(1,1)$ entry $\approx +0.18 > 0$, completely violating the LMI.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $\sigma_n(\fA_j)$ in the definition of $\mu$ with the spectral abscissa of the symmetric part, $-\lambda_{\max}(\frac{\fA_j+\fA_j^\T}{2}) = \lambda_{\min}(-\frac{\fA_j+\fA_j^\T}{2}) > 0$, requiring $\mu \ge \max_{j\in\switchingSet} \frac{\sigma_1(\fA_j)}{\lambda_{\min}(-\frac{\fA_j+\fA_j^\T}{2})} \|\fX - \tilde\fX\|_2$.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 3.5 does not guarantee that the perturbed Gramian $\hat\fX$ satisfies the LMI (2.5a). Consequently, quadratic stability and error bounds based on this perturbation are not guaranteed.
issues.title: Invalid LMI satisfaction guarantee via condition number perturbation
issues.why_classification: A contained correction replacing $\sigma_n(\fA_j)$ with $\lambda_{\min}(-\frac{\fA_j+\fA_j^\T}{2})$ restores the proof and conclusion without altering the overall reduction architecture, though it weakens the allowable parameter regime and perturbation size.

issues.failure_explanation: In the proof of Lemma 4.2 (Appendix A.1), the step below (A.3) replaces $\lambda_1(\fM_c)\bfX_c(t)^\T \fSigma^{-2} \bfX_c(t)$ with $\lambda_1(\fM_c)\frac{1}{\sigma^2}\|\bfX_c(t)\|_2^2$. Because $\fSigma^{-2} \preceq \frac{1}{\sigma^2}\fI$, this inequality holds only when $\lambda_1(\fM_c) \ge 0$. In the intended regime where the LMIs are strictly satisfied, $\lambda_1(\fM_c) < 0$, which reverses the inequality to $\lambda_1(\fM_c)\bfX_c(t)^\T \fSigma^{-2} \bfX_c(t) \ge \lambda_1(\fM_c)\frac{1}{\sigma^2}\|\bfX_c(t)\|_2^2$. Consequently, $\gleH_{c,\switch}$ becomes negative and improperly subtracts from the upper bound in (4.7), making the claimed bound invalid.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $\lambda_1(\fM_c)$ and $\lambda_1(\fM_o)$ in the definitions of $\gleH_{c,\switch}$ and $\gleH_{o,\switch}$ with $\max\{0, \lambda_1(\fM_c)\}$ and $\max\{0, \lambda_1(\fM_o)\}$.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 4.2 does not provide a valid upper bound on the output error whenever $\lambda_1(\fM_c) < 0$.
issues.title: Reversed inequality in single-step balanced truncation error bound for negative LMI eigenvalues
issues.why_classification: The failure is resolved by a standard local modification taking the positive part of the maximum eigenvalue, which preserves the proof technique, the result, and its advertised scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proof follows directly by applying the sub-additivity of the square root function to \Cref{teo5} and standard balance truncation error arguments; see, for instance, \cite[Sec.~7]{PetWL13}.

issues.failure_explanation: In Theorem 4.4, the error bound in (4.8) contains the term $-\sum_{k=r+1}^{\tilde n} \gleG_{c,o,\switch}(s_{k+1}, s_k)^{1/2} H(-\gleG_{c,o,\switch}(s_{k+1}, s_k))$. When $-\gleG_{c,o,\switch} > 0$, the Heaviside factor is 1, but $\gleG_{c,o,\switch} < 0$, which makes $\gleG_{c,o,\switch}^{1/2}$ strictly imaginary. Furthermore, applying subadditivity of the square root to the term $-\gleG_{c,o,\switch}$ appearing inside the radicand in Lemma 4.2 requires adding $(-\gleG_{c,o,\switch})^{1/2}$, whereas the expression in (4.8) subtracts it, which would improperly diminish an upper bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the term $-\gleG_{c,o,\switch}(s_{k+1}, s_k)^{1/2} H(-\gleG_{c,o,\switch}(s_{k+1}, s_k))$ in (4.8) with $+\left(-\gleG_{c,o,\switch}(s_{k+1}, s_k)\right)^{1/2} H(-\gleG_{c,o,\switch}(s_{k+1}, s_k))$.
issues.overall_effect: The cumulative error bound in Theorem 4.4 is ill-defined (evaluates to a complex number) whenever $-\gleG_{c,o,\switch} > 0$, and invalid as an upper bound due to the negative sign.
issues.title: Imaginary and subtracted error contribution from piecewise Gramians in Theorem 4.4
issues.why_classification: This is a direct algebraic correction of the subadditivity application that preserves the stated bound and all claims.
